query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Machine learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately and efficiently determine the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys across the family.
generation.intervention: Application of machine learning potentials trained on ab initio data
generation.conditions: Melting temperature range of high-entropy alloys
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic arrangement and bonding in high-entropy alloys
generation.mechanism: Ab initio molecular dynamics and density functional theory calculations
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean absolute error in predicted melting temperature less than 50 K, and mean absolute error in predicted enthalpy and entropy of fusion less than 10% relative to experimental values
generation.boundary: High-entropy alloys with up to 10 principal elements
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in transferability of machine learning potentials to new high-entropy alloys, and uncertainty in accuracy of ab initio data used for training

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of predicted thermodynamic properties with experimental values for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mean absolute error in predicted melting temperature exceeds 100 K, or the mean absolute error in predicted enthalpy and entropy of fusion exceeds 20% relative to experimental values, the hypothesis is falsified

precedents.problem: Discovering lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys
precedents.outcome: Identification of alloys with yield strengths of 1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C and 607 ± 22 MPa at 700 °C

precedents.problem: Understanding the effect of sintering temperature on microstructure evolution, phase formation, and mechanical properties of CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy
precedents.outcome: Compressive strength of all sintered samples ranged from 2700 to 2870 MPa, with low plasticity attributed to brittle Laves phases and oxides at grain boundaries

precedents.problem: Investigating the wear behavior of AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy under reciprocating wear conditions at elevated temperatures
precedents.outcome: The alloy exhibited a distinct reduction in wear depth at 800 °C, with the highest wear resistance observed at 900 °C

precedents.problem: Understanding the effect of small additions of hafnium and molybdenum on microstructural characteristics and high-temperature mechanical properties of Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 high-entropy alloy
precedents.outcome: Directional solidification increased ultimate tensile strength by a factor of 1.5–1.8 compared to conventional casting at temperatures up to 700 °C

precedents.problem: Investigating the tensile and creep properties of Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 high entropy alloy and the effect of gravity casting versus suction-assisted casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP)
precedents.outcome: The HIP process induced the formation of a secondary Hexagonal Close Packed (HCP) phase in addition to the initial Body Centered Cubic (BCC) phase
